subject: Cadenza.ai post-call: inference requirements, SLOs & deployment sketch
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@cadenza.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cadenza.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: inference requirements, SLOs & deployment sketch

Thanks for the call today — appreciated the clarity on where Cadenza.ai is with the MLP-based summarization feature. Short recap and proposed next steps below.

Key pain points you highlighted
- 200–400ms p95 latency target on short text (avg 150 tokens) for end-user generation flows.
- Sustained peak throughput ~250–350 QPS during batch windows and marketing spikes.
- Data residency in us-west and strict audit logs / retention controls.
- Model output consistency: occasional hallucinations currently breaking workflows.

Goals we heard
- Production-grade inference by Q4 with rollback and canary controls.
- Unit cost reduction vs current DIY fleet (target 35% lower cost/token).
- SOC2 evidence and tighter KMS integration for encrypted logs.

Technical notes / initial recommendations
- Model candidates: evaluate quantized Llama2-70B and a 13B fallback for latency tiers.
- Deployment topology: Dedicated capacity pool in us-west-2 with autoscaling + burst lane to hosted capacity for peak bursts.
- KV / prefix caching: enable per-customer prefix cache to reduce repeated context costs; estimate 12–18% token savings given your prompt reuse.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with 25–30ms batching window for throughput/latency balance.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to 13B when p95 latency or queue depth exceeds threshold.

Open items we promised to follow up on
1) Sizing sketch (initial GPU counts / memory) — Karthik to produce by EOD today.
2) SOC2 questionnaire — attached (Priya, please skip to section 2 for logs/retention ask).
3) Mutual action plan + procurement timeline — I attached a blank MAP.
4) Deep-dive call (ops + infra) — propose Tue 9/2 10am PT; please confirm.

Attachments: Cadenza_SOC2_Questions.pdf, initial-topology-sketch.png, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks,
--
David Kim
Enterprise Solutions (West)
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@cadenza.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cadenza.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference requirements, SLOs & deployment sketch

David — thanks for the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- The 200–400ms p95 is a hard goal for interactive sessions; for batched background jobs we can tolerate up to 1s.
- Peak QPS of 350 is a reasonable buffer to plan for. Our spike pattern is very bursty (short-lived 10–15min spikes).
- Procurement: legal wants to see an initial run-of-service SLA and proof of SOC2 scope covering logs + KMS before committing to a 12‑month Dedicated purchase.

I reviewed the topology sketch and like the dedicated pool + hosted burst idea. A few asks:
1) Can you confirm encrypted KV cache behavior (does caching store plaintext user inputs or only token IDs)?
2) Can you share a rough cost delta for L2-70B quantized vs 13B per 1M tokens (ballpark)?

Happy to take Tue 9/2 10am PT. Priya and I will invite our cloud security lead if we can.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Product
Cadenza.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference requirements, SLOs & deployment sketch

Looping in a short technical sizing and action list (quick, rough numbers so sales has something concrete for MAP).

Sizing assumptions
- Workload: avg request 150 tokens in, 200 tokens out; 350 QPS peak (burstable).
- Model: Llama2‑70B quantized to 4-bit (int4) for main tier; Llama2‑13B int8 for fallback.

Preliminary capacity sketch (us-west-2 dedicated pool)
- 70B int4 baseline: 8 x A100‑80GB equiv nodes for sustained 250 QPS with headroom (can hit ~300 QPS with burst).
- Burst lane to hosted: allow overflow routing for +50–100 QPS to hosted instances (costlier but keeps latency within SLO).
- Fallback 13B: hosted or smaller dedicated set of 2 x 80GB nodes for very low-latency routes.

Latency tuning notes
- Use short batching window (20–30ms) and priority routing for interactive sessions to keep p95 < 250ms.
- KV/prefix cache should store model tokens and cache keys encrypted at rest; we recommend cache encryption keys scoped per-Customer KMS to meet your controls.

Next technical deliverables (I will own)
- Detailed capacity worksheet (nodes, GPUs, expected cost range) by Mon 8/31 EOD.
- Short note on quantization accuracy tradeoffs and candidate eval prompts.

Attaching a quick topology sketch and a link to the small-run cost estimator (internal).

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

- 9/7: Redwood sends draft SLA and example contract language for procurement review.
- 9/14: Target pilot start (2–4 week pilot, dedicated pool + host-burst) pending legal/procurement sign-off.

Immediate asks for Cadenza

- If legal can share must-have SLA terms before 9/4, we'll try to bake them into the example contract.

Procurement & trial notes

- DocuSign link to initial NDA/statement will be sent after your confirmation; I've attached a MAP workbook to populate owners/dates.

If that captures everything, Sanjay/Priya — can you confirm the 9/2 time and whether your security lead will join?

Thanks,
